evidence: "1. Workload metrics — what the system is being asked to do. Requests per second (rps) and the token profile (input length, output length, context length). These are the independent variables — the offered load; we do not control them, we characterize them. Admitted concurrency is a serving/scheduler state (Little's law), not a workload input. Fig 6.1's workload box lists concurrency alongside rps and the token profile: read that entry as offered concurrency — the arrival-side λ that the traffic offers — not as admitted or queued concurrency, which sits on the serving/scheduler side with queue depth."

The body text now declares that Fig 6.1's workload box 'lists concurrency alongside rps and the token profile' and instructs the reader to reinterpret it as offered/arrival-side concurrency.
